SALICYLATE OVERDOSE 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
CLINICAL FEATURES 
May take up to 6 hours to appear 
 
* MINIMAL (<150 mg/kg): minimal symptoms 
* MODERATE (150-300mg/kg): Hyperpnoea; vomiting; nausea; tinnitus 
* SEVERE (>300mg/kg):  Metabolic acidosis, seizures, coma, hypotension,   
                                             pulmonary oedema, hyperthermia 
* LETHAL (>500mg/kg) 
* CHRONIC: Common in elderly pts, non-specific delirium, confusion,  
                       fever, unexplained acidosis. 
GENERAL APPROACH 
 
•
Triage to RESUS AREA, even if patient initially appears well  
•
Rapid ABC assessment, 2 IV lines, monitors, HGT, VBG, urine bHCG, ECG 
•
Correct electrolyte abnormalities 
•
Crystalloid fluid bolus 20mg/kg if hypotensive 
•
Comprehensive history and examination, including: 
§
Amount and time of ingestion, co-ingestants 
§
Comorbidities, chronic medications, symptoms prior to arrival 
•
Document specific features of toxicity 
•
Further investigations: FBC, U&E, LFT, Paracetamol/Salicylate level, urine tox screen 
 
***LEVELS CORRELATE POORLY WITH SEVERITY OF TOXICITY, BUT SERIAL LEVELS CAN BE USED TO 
MONITOR RESPONSE OF TREATMENT*** 
         **NEUROGLYCOPENIA CAN OCCUR EVEN AT NORMAL HGT LEVELS** 
SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT 
 
DECONTAMINATION:  
§
If > 150mg/kg ingested - 50g activated charcoal up to 8 hours post ingestion 
§
If > 300mg/kg ingested - SECURE AIRWAY PRIOR TO ACTIVATED CHARCOAL 
§
Consider MDAC if salicylate levels continue to rise 
ENHANCED ELIMINATION: 
§
Urinary and serum alkalinisation with sodium bicarbonate 1ml/kg IV of 8.5% Sodabic 
§
Goal serum pH 7.45 – 7.55, urine pH >7.5 
§
Haemodialysis – very effective but seldom required 
SEIZURES:  
§
IV benzodiazepines 
§
Monitor for arrhythmias / hypoglycaemia as cause 
INTUBATION CONSIDERATIONS:  
§
Avoid intubation if possible à associated with high peri-intubation mortality 
§
Consider Sodabic boluses prior to intubation to counteract metabolic acidosis.  
§
Minimise apnoeic period to avoid worsening acidosis 
§
Match patient’s respiratory rate to maintain respiratory alkalosis 
DISPOSITION 
 
•
GIT consult 
•
Will likely require ICU/High care 
•
Continue serial ECG and VBG monitoring in ED 
BLOOD GAS FEATURES 
 
* Respiratory alkalosis – direct stimulation of respiratory centres 
* Metabolic acidosis (HAGMA) – lactic acidosis due to uncoupling of  
   oxidative phosphorylation 
* Hypokalaemia 
* Hyper/hypoglycaemia 
 
Winter’s formula:  1.5 x HCO3 + 8 ± 2 = expected CO2  
(if pure metabolic acidosis) 
Dr J du Plessis / Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
